section: India's energy resources and import dependence - crude oil, coal, gas import share; energy security
subsections: Import-substitution fuels - methanol, DME, ethanol, CBG

accepted.s:
Methanol used as an import-substitution fuel can be produced from which of the following feedstocks?
1. Biomass
2. Natural gas
3. High-ash coal
4. Agricultural residue
5. Carbon dioxide from thermal power plants
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Methanol can be produced from biomass, natural gas, high-ash coal, agricultural residue and carbon dioxide captured from thermal power plants.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when every listed feedstock belongs to the same production pathway.
accepted.sec: Import-substitution fuels - methanol, DME, ethanol, CBG

accepted.s: With reference to methanol as an energy fuel, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It is used exclusively as a substitute for natural gas in fertiliser plants.
It can replace petrol and diesel in transport and can also be used in boilers and generator sets.
It can replace coal in blast furnaces but cannot be used for cooking.
It can be used only for electricity generation and not for transport.
accepted.x: Methanol can replace petrol and diesel in transport, and it can also be used in diesel generator sets, boilers and partly in LPG and kerosene applications for cooking.
accepted.tq: Apply the fuel’s listed uses across transport, power equipment and cooking rather than choosing an exclusive use.
accepted.sec: Import-substitution fuels - methanol, DME, ethanol, CBG

accepted.s: Di-methyl ether (DME) is chemically obtained by
o: removing one water molecule from two methanol molecules
adding one water molecule to two methanol molecules
removing two oxygen molecules from one ethanol molecule
combining methane with carbon dioxide under pressure
accepted.x: DME is formed by removing one water molecule from two methanol molecules.
accepted.tq: Break the chemical description into its operation—two methanol molecules minus one water molecule.
accepted.sec: Import-substitution fuels - methanol, DME, ethanol, CBG

accepted.s:
DME can substitute which of the following fuels or applications?
1. Propane in LPG
2. Diesel in slow-RPM engines
3. Petrol in aircraft engines
4. Coal in thermal power plants
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: DME can substitute propane in LPG and diesel in slow-RPM engines. Its stated applications do not include replacing petrol in aircraft engines or coal in thermal power plants.
accepted.tq: Find the two specific substitution relationships and reject broader fuel-swapping claims.
accepted.sec: Import-substitution fuels - methanol, DME, ethanol, CBG

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Ethanol Blended Petrol in India:
1. Pilot projects for ethanol blending began in 2001.
2. The government resolved to sell 5 per cent ethanol-blended petrol from 1 January 2003.
3. The initial resolution covered nine States and four Union Territories.
4. Ethanol blending was approximately 1.53 per cent in 2013–14.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: pilots began in 2001; 5 per cent blending was resolved from 1 January 2003 in nine States and four Union Territories; and blending was about 1.53 per cent in 2013–14.
accepted.tq: Check each date, percentage and geographical coverage independently before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Import-substitution fuels - methanol, DME, ethanol, CBG

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the progress of ethanol blending mentioned in the energy policy context?
o: Only E5 was achieved after the scheduled target and no farmer payments were made.
E20 was achieved ahead of schedule and farmers received payments exceeding ₹1,29,032 crore.
E20 was abandoned and farmers received less than ₹1,000 crore.
E20 was restricted to Union Territories and payments were made only to oil companies.
accepted.x: E20 was achieved ahead of schedule, and farmers received payments of over ₹1,29,032 crore.
accepted.tq: Match the programme milestone with the associated monetary figure; the precise amount is the key discriminator.
accepted.sec: Import-substitution fuels - methanol, DME, ethanol, CBG

accepted.s: The Compressed Biogas Obligation for consumption of CNG/PNG in the City Gas Distribution sector is scheduled as
accepted.x: The CBO is 1 per cent, 3 per cent and 4 per cent in FY 2025–26, 2026–27 and 2027–28 respectively, rising to 5 per cent from 2028–29.
accepted.tq: Track the year-wise progression and identify the option preserving the exact sequence.
accepted.sec: Import-substitution fuels - methanol, DME, ethanol, CBG

accepted.s: The principal objective of introducing Compressed Biogas Obligation in the City Gas Distribution sector is to
o: increase coal imports for power generation
replace all petrol vehicles with electric vehicles
substitute imports of liquefied natural gas
increase the import of LPG cylinders
accepted.x: The CBO is intended to promote compressed biogas and substitute LNG imports.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated import-substitution objective rather than a general clean-energy benefit.
accepted.sec: Import-substitution fuels - methanol, DME, ethanol, CBG

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Fuel blend)
A. M15
B. 20% DME in LPG

List-II (Stated benefit)
1. Saves approximately ₹6,000 crore per year
2. Cuts gasoline/crude imports by at least 15%
3. Saves ₹50–100 per LPG cylinder
4. Cuts particulate matter, NOx and SOx by 20%

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: M15 is associated with at least a 15 per cent cut in gasoline/crude imports and a 20 per cent reduction in PM, NOx and SOx. A 20 per cent DME blend in LPG is associated with savings of about ₹6,000 crore annually and ₹50–100 per cylinder.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair: M15 directly corresponds to a 15 per cent import reduction.
accepted.sec: Import-substitution fuels - methanol, DME, ethanol, CBG

accepted.s: The employment potential associated with the methanol economy is stated to be close to
accepted.x: The employment potential associated with the methanol economy is close to 5 million jobs.
accepted.tq: Use the order of magnitude carefully; the nearby zeroes distinguish million-scale estimates.
accepted.sec: Import-substitution fuels - methanol, DME, ethanol, CBG

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s Phase I strategic petroleum reserves:
1. They are located in underground rock caverns.
2. The sites include Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur.
3. Their total capacity is 5.33 million metric tonnes.
4. At full capacity they provide about 9.5 days of cover.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Phase I reserves are underground rock caverns at Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur, with a total capacity of 5.33 MMT and about 9.5 days of cover at full capacity.
accepted.tq: Combine location, storage form, capacity and coverage only after verifying each numerical detail.
accepted.sec: Energy security tools - SPR, exploration, overseas equity, diversification

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a strategic petroleum reserve site with its State and capacity?
accepted.x: Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh has a stated capacity of 1.33 MMT. Mangaluru and Padur are in Karnataka, while Padur’s capacity is 2.5 MMT.
accepted.tq: Check the place–State–capacity triple; the wrong options swap either the State or the capacity.
accepted.sec: Energy security tools - SPR, exploration, overseas equity, diversification

accepted.s: The International Energy Agency norm for strategic oil reserves is approximately
accepted.x: The IEA norm referred to for strategic oil reserves is 90 days of cover, compared with about 9.5 days at India’s Phase I full capacity.
accepted.tq: Separate India’s current reserve coverage from the international benchmark.
accepted.sec: Energy security tools - SPR, exploration, overseas equity, diversification

accepted.s: At the reported utilisation level of 64 per cent, India’s Phase I strategic petroleum reserves held approximately
o: 5.33 MT and provided about 9.5 days of cover
9 MT and provided about 56 days of cover
1.33 MT and provided about 2 days of cover
3.37 MT and provided about 5 days of cover
accepted.x: Actual stocks were approximately 3.37 MT at 64 per cent utilisation, providing about five days of cover. The 5.33 MMT and 9.5-day figures refer to full capacity.
accepted.tq: Distinguish capacity from actual utilisation and compare full-capacity cover with current cover.
accepted.sec: Energy security tools - SPR, exploration, overseas equity, diversification

accepted.s:
Which of the following sites are associated with Phase II of India’s strategic petroleum reserve programme?
1. Chandikhol
2. Padur
3. Bikaner
4. Rajkot
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Phase II was approved for Chandikhol in Odisha and Padur in Karnataka. Bikaner and Rajkot were proposed sites, not approved Phase II sites.
accepted.tq: Separate approved sites from merely proposed sites; this is a common status-based trap.
accepted.sec: Energy security tools - SPR, exploration, overseas equity, diversification

accepted.s: The proposed decade-long strategic fuel programme would add storage capacity in which combination?
o: 28 MT LNG, 9 MT crude and 4 MT LPG
20 MT crude, 15 MT LNG and 6 MT LPG
28 MT crude, 9 MT LNG and 4 MT LPG
accepted.x: The proposed programme totals 41 MT, comprising 28 MT of crude, 9 MT of LNG and 4 MT of LPG.
accepted.tq: Use the total as a check on the three component figures: 28 + 9 + 4 equals 41 MT.
accepted.sec: Energy security tools - SPR, exploration, overseas equity, diversification

accepted.s: The proposed strategic fuel programme is expected to provide approximately
o: two months of crude, 56 days of LNG and six weeks of LPG cover
90 days of crude, 90 days of LNG and 90 days of LPG cover
six weeks of crude, two months of LNG and 56 days of LPG cover
five days of crude, 9.5 days of LNG and six weeks of LPG cover
accepted.x: The proposed programme is estimated to cover about two months of crude, 56 days of LNG and six weeks of LPG requirements.
accepted.tq: Match each fuel with its distinct coverage period instead of treating all storage as equivalent.
accepted.sec: Energy security tools - SPR, exploration, overseas equity, diversification

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct regarding India’s hydrocarbon storage position?
o: LPG semi-strategic caverns have a capacity of approximately 0.14 MT.
India’s underground natural-gas storage capacity is greater than its crude-oil storage capacity.
India has no underground natural-gas storage facility mentioned in the assessment.
The total oil stock is approximately 74 days.
accepted.x: The assessment states that there is no underground natural-gas storage. LPG semi-strategic caverns are about 0.14 MT and total oil stock is about 74 days.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that directly contradicts the stated absence of underground natural-gas storage.
accepted.sec: Energy security tools - SPR, exploration, overseas equity, diversification

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the Four A’s of energy security?
accepted.x: The Four A’s are availability, accessibility, affordability and acceptability.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact official wording; similar-looking administrative terms are distractors.
accepted.sec: Energy security tools - SPR, exploration, overseas equity, diversification

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. HELP provides a single licence for all hydrocarbons.
2. OALP is associated with upstream exploration and production.
3. ONGC Videsh is the overseas arm of ONGC.
4. Overseas acreages can augment India’s oil and gas supply.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: HELP provides a unified licence for hydrocarbons; OALP concerns upstream exploration; ONGC Videsh is ONGC’s overseas arm; and overseas acreages help augment supply.
accepted.tq: Test the institutional roles together, while avoiding the trap of treating overseas acquisition as domestic production.
accepted.sec: Energy security tools - SPR, exploration, overseas equity, diversification

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly matches a resource with the quantity stated for India?
accepted.x: India’s stated thorium resource is 3,60,000 tonnes, approximately 25 per cent of the world’s total, while natural uranium is 70,000 tonnes.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the two radioactive resources by matching the larger figure with thorium.
accepted.sec: Domestic reserves - number game

accepted.s: With reference to India’s sedimentary basins, which one of the following is correct?
o: All 26 basins are currently producing hydrocarbons.
Only 7 sedimentary basins exist, all of which are producing.
Of 26 sedimentary basins, only 7 are producing.
Of 26 sedimentary basins, 19 are producing and 7 are non-producing.
accepted.x: India has 26 sedimentary basins, of which only 7 are producing according to the stated figures.
accepted.tq: Watch the reversal between the total number of basins and the number that are producing.
accepted.sec: Domestic reserves - number game

accepted.s: India is described as the world’s ______ largest holder of coal reserves in the current estimate referred to.
accepted.x: The current estimate identifies India as the world’s fifth-largest holder of coal reserves; an older estimate had placed it fourth.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the current ranking from the older alternative ranking.
accepted.sec: Domestic reserves - number game

accepted.s: India’s crude import bill in July 2026 was approximately
accepted.x: India’s crude import bill was approximately $13.7 billion in July 2026.
accepted.tq: Separate the monetary import bill from the physical import volume of 21.4 MMT.
accepted.sec: Energy import bill - trade deficit impact

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s petroleum trade in July 2026:
1. The crude import bill increased by 41 per cent year-on-year.
2. Crude import volume was 21.4 MMT.
3. Petroleum product exports rose by 10 per cent to 5.5 MMT.
4. India has been a net petroleum product exporter since 2001–02.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct: the bill rose 41 per cent year-on-year, volume was 21.4 MMT, product exports rose 10 per cent to 5.5 MMT, and India has been a net product exporter since 2001–02.
accepted.tq: Verify the date, percentage, volume and long-term trade-status statement separately before choosing all four.
accepted.sec: Energy import bill - trade deficit impact

accepted.s: India’s crude import volume in July 2026 increased by approximately
accepted.x: The crude import volume was 21.4 MMT, representing a year-on-year increase of 13.3 per cent. The 41 per cent figure refers to the increase in the import bill.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the percentage change in value from the percentage change in physical volume.
accepted.sec: Energy import bill - trade deficit impact

accepted.s: India became an association country of the International Energy Agency in
accepted.x: India became an IEA association country in 2017 and is not a full member.
accepted.tq: Use the status distinction—association country versus full member—along with the year.
accepted.sec: Energy partnerships - IEA, GBA, IEF

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about India’s energy partnerships is correct?
o: India is a full member of the IEA and does not participate in the IEF.
India works with OPEC through an Energy Dialogue and also engages with the IEF and IEA.
India’s energy cooperation is limited to the Global Biofuels Alliance.
India works only with the IEA and has no energy dialogue with OPEC.
accepted.x: India engages with OPEC through an Energy Dialogue and also works with the International Energy Forum and the IEA. It is an IEA association country, not a full member.
accepted.tq: Reject exclusive wording and identify the option listing all three stated energy partnerships.
accepted.sec: Energy partnerships - IEA, GBA, IEF

accepted.s: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched in 2023 during
o: India’s presidency of the International Energy Forum
the United Nations Climate Conference hosted by India
accepted.x: The Global Biofuels Alliance was launched in 2023 during India’s G20 presidency.
accepted.tq: Pair the launch year with the correct international presidency rather than a neighbouring energy institution.
accepted.sec: Energy partnerships - IEA, GBA, IEF

accepted.s: The Global Biofuels Alliance comprises which of the following membership figures?
accepted.x: The Global Biofuels Alliance has 32 countries and 14 international organisations as the stated participants.
accepted.tq: Keep the country count and organisation count in their respective order.
accepted.sec: Energy partnerships - IEA, GBA, IEF

accepted.s: The secretariat of the International Energy Forum is located at
accepted.x: The International Energy Forum secretariat is located in Riyadh.
accepted.tq: Use the headquarters-location distinction among major energy institutions.
accepted.sec: Energy partnerships - IEA, GBA, IEF

accepted.s: India hosted the 16th ministerial meeting of the International Energy Forum in
accepted.x: India hosted the 16th IEF ministerial meeting in 2018.
accepted.tq: Match the ordinal meeting number with its year, avoiding the nearby IEA and GBA dates.
accepted.sec: Energy partnerships - IEA, GBA, IEF

accepted.s:
Consider the following as focus areas of Hydrocarbon Vision 2025:
1. Higher domestic hydrocarbon output and acquisition of equity oil abroad
2. Strategic and buffer stocks
3. Appraisal of all sedimentary basins
4. Globally competitive refining
5. Free market and competition
6. Better fuel quality
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All six listed items are focus areas: domestic output and overseas equity oil, strategic and buffer stocks, appraisal of sedimentary basins, competitive refining, market competition and improved fuel quality.
accepted.tq: Recognise the comprehensive policy-list option when every item belongs to the same long-term framework.
accepted.sec: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 - focus areas

accepted.s: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 was adopted by the Government of India in
accepted.x: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 was adopted by the Government of India in 2000.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the adoption year from the policy’s horizon year in its title.
accepted.sec: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 - focus areas

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a focus area associated with Hydrocarbon Vision 2025?
o: Complete prohibition of private participation in hydrocarbons
accepted.x: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 promotes a free market and competition; it does not seek complete prohibition of private participation. The other three are stated focus areas.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the policy’s market-oriented approach.
accepted.sec: Hydrocarbon Vision 2025 - focus areas
